construction: Constructed by opus-rules-researcher (M02) on 2026-09-23 directly from the captured source text (docs/rules/sources/ecfr-14cfr260.txt, usc-49-42305.txt, ecfr-14cfr399.80l-excerpt.txt, federal-web-pages-excerpts.md) and the spec. Not generated by, run through, or checked against any evaluator code.

conventions.fact_encoding: facts.<name> = {type, value, state}; state in {user_confirmed, observed, derived, extracted_candidate, conflicting, missing, assumption} (README 'Fixture format'). money = {amount_minor:int, currency:ISO-4217}. datetime = ISO-8601 with UTC offset. Missing facts are state=missing with value null; missing is never false.
conventions.source_state: verified_current unless the case or variant sets source.last_verified_on; refresh window for R02 is 30 days (spec header).
conventions.business_days: Mon-Fri excluding 5 U.S.C. 6103 federal holidays (2026: Oct 12 Columbus Day, Nov 11 Veterans Day, Nov 26 Thanksgiving, Dec 25). Count starts the day after the anchor date; the Nth business day is the last compliant day.
conventions.deadline_meaning: For R02 every computed deadline is the CARRIER's refund-issuance deadline (tracking/escalation), not a consumer filing deadline.
conventions.carrier_names: Fictional carrier codes (XA, XB) are used so fixtures do not imply real events.
conventions.loader: A case has EITHER a top-level `expected` OR an `expected` on every variant. `clock` (and optional `source`) may be set on the case or on a variant; a variant value overrides the case value. `facts_from: <case id>` + `facts_override: {...}` means: copy that case's facts, then replace the named facts. A variant's `change` object replaces the named facts for that variant only. Every `facts` value is an object; no prose placeholders.
conventions.fact_states: user_confirmed | observed | derived | extracted_candidate | conflicting | missing | assumption. Contract §2.5 mapping: user_confirmed→confirmed, observed→observed, derived→derived, extracted_candidate→candidate, conflicting→conflicting, missing→missing (value null), assumption→assumption-class candidate. D147(2)/X1: `eligible` requires every decisive fact to be user_confirmed, or observed/derived from confirmed facts; an extracted_candidate decisive fact caps the outcome at likely_eligible_missing_evidence (the case lists it in expected.unconfirmed_decisive_facts). Since M2D the baseline cases use user_confirmed for decisive facts (the state after the user's fact review); each file has explicit cap variants.
conventions.conflicting: D152/D154 (README cross-pack rule 3): conflict_kind 'candidates' → different outcomes or amounts = needs_facts; same outcome and amount = capped at likely_eligible_missing_evidence (fact listed in unconfirmed_decisive_facts). conflict_kind 'confirmed_vs_observed' / 'confirmed_vs_confirmed' → manual_review. A conflicting or extracted-only deadline anchor never gives a firm date: deadline.date = null, status disputed_anchor / unknown_anchor, and (user-obligor paths only) advisory_act_by from the earliest candidate.
conventions.not_yet_due: D147(6)/X3: a path that is not ripe yet has outcome not_yet_due with expected.reevaluate_at (ISO date) or expected.reevaluate_when (event); never not_eligible.
conventions.missing_source: X5: a variant with source.record = 'missing' means no current source record exists for the pack → source_unverified.

cases.title: Cancellation, rebooking offered and rejected, credit card, carrier is merchant of record

service_type.note: D253(3): recorded so this case's expected outcome is preserved; an unknown service type caps the result at likely eligible (R02-15)

amount.formula: fare + taxes + ancillary fees - already refunded

deadline.semantics: 7 business days after the anchor date 2026-10-01 (rejection); 2026-10-12 is a federal holiday and is skipped; last compliant day inclusive
not computable: anchored on the ticket agent receiving the carrier's eligibility information (399.80(l), 260.6(d)), which the consumer cannot observe

expected.next_action: request the refund from the ticket agent (refund is owed upon request, not automatically)

justification.reasoning: When a ticket agent is the merchant of record, 399.80(l) makes the agent's failure to refund 'upon request' the violation; the timing is keyed to the agent receiving carrier information.

value.note: round-trip fare; no per-segment split on the receipt

amount.reason: 260.6(a)(1) does not address a partly flown itinerary (spec §8, assumption A4)

justification.reasoning: Eligibility for the cancelled return segment is established; the amount for a partly used round trip is not determinable from the text.
Decisive facts extracted but not confirmed cap the outcome at likely_eligible.

expected.reason: deemed-request date 2024-09-15 is before the refund-provision compliance date 2024-10-28 (spec §16 step 1b)

justification.reasoning: v1 does not evaluate events before the compliance date.

A cancelled covered flight + consumer rejection of rebooking is a deemed refund request (260.6(a)(2)(ii)). The carrier is merchant of record, so the refund is automatic and must include taxes and ancillary fees. The credit-card payment deadline is 7 business days after the earliest request date.

cases.title: Domestic schedule change — arrival threshold boundary at 3 hours

service_type.note: D253(3): recorded so this case's expected outcome is preserved; an unknown service type caps the result at likely eligible (R02-15)

expected.note: Below 'three or more hours'; no other significance criterion met. A carrier customer-service commitment (R15) is a separate question.

justification.reasoning: Criterion (2): 'three or more hours for domestic itineraries ... after the original scheduled arrival time'. Exactly 3:00 qualifies; 2:59 does not. Compare absolute instants.

cases.title: Significant change accepted — passenger flew the changed flight

expected.note: The change was significant (3h01m) but the passenger flew it. Show R15 (carrier commitment) only as a separate, carrier-specific path — never as a cash-compensation right.

justification.reasoning: The refund duty applies only where the consumer 'chooses not to ... Fly on the significantly delayed or changed flight or accept rebooking'. DOT: 'If you chose to take a significantly delayed/changed flight ... you are not entitled to a refund under DOT rules.'

cases.title: Significant change notified; no confirmed acceptance decision; changed flight not yet departed
cases.mission_domain_fixture: flight change without confirmed acceptance decision

expected.question: Did you accept the new schedule, reject it, or not respond? If you do not respond and do not take the changed flight, DOT rules treat that as a refund request once the flight departs.
expected.note: Must NOT be 'eligible' (decision unknown) and must NOT be 'not_eligible' (missing is not false).

justification.reasoning: The change (3h30m) is significant, but eligibility turns on the consumer's decision: rejection, non-response followed by departure, or acceptance. None is known yet.

cases.title: One-hour operational delay (revised schedule +1h05m); passenger flew
cases.mission_domain_fixture: short delay without an independently qualifying remedy

forbidden_outputs: any cash-compensation opportunity for delay inconvenience
expected.note: Revised scheduled arrival +1h05m meets no significance criterion and the passenger flew. No federal delay compensation exists (ANPRM withdrawn 2025-11-17). R15 may be shown only as 'check the carrier's customer-service commitments'.

justification.reasoning: A 1h05m delay meets no significance criterion and the passenger flew. Amenities for controllable disruptions are carrier commitments (DOT-REF-5), not a refund right.

service_type.note: D253(3): recorded so this case's expected outcome is preserved; an unknown service type caps the result at likely eligible (R02-15)

expected.note: A same-day delay whose revised schedule is 3h20m late is a significantly delayed flight; the passenger declined it.

justification.reasoning: 260.2 covers a 'delay or change'; criterion (2) applies to the revised schedule.

expected.reason: revised schedule +2h50m (below 3 h) but the flight actually arrived +3h10m: statute 'arrives' vs regulation 'scheduled to arrive' (spec §4)

justification.reasoning: The two first-party texts point to different events; only this conclusion is blocked.

cases.title: Cancellation, rejection, paid by DEBIT card — 20 calendar days; DOT page conflict disclosed

service_type.note: D253(3): recorded so this case's expected outcome is preserved; an unknown service type caps the result at likely eligible (R02-15)

deadline.semantics: 20 calendar days after 2026-10-01 per 260.2 ('cash, check, debit card, or other forms')
deadline.disclosed_conflict: DOT consumer page (DOT-REF-3) says '20 business days (for cash purchases)'; read literally that would be 2026-10-30. Not used; shown as a disclosed source conflict.

expected.note: The debit-card payment method changes only the refund timer, not eligibility. It must not be routed to Regulation E.

justification.reasoning: The regulation lists debit card among the 20-calendar-day forms of payment. DOT-REF-1 (same page, same event) also says 20 calendar days; DOT-REF-3 is an internal inconsistency (spec §15 L2).

cases.title: Contradictory changed-arrival times straddle the 3-hour threshold

expected.question: Two documents show different new arrival times (4:10 pm and 3:40 pm). Which is the carrier's latest schedule?
forbidden_outputs: picking the candidate favourable to the user

justification.reasoning: One candidate meets criterion (2), the other does not. The conflict is material and must be resolved by the user or a newer carrier record (mission §8 source/fact disagreement).

deadline.semantics: 7 business days after the confirmed rejection on 2026-09-22; applies once the change is confirmed as significant

expected.note: Both candidates are ≥ 3 h and give the same outcome and amount (22,500): the conflict is not material, but the fact is unconfirmed (D154 5c).

justification.reasoning: Same outcome under every candidate; confirmation still required for eligible.

cases.title: Intra-Europe flight on a non-US carrier with no US point

expected.note: Not a covered flight (no US point). 'Unsupported' is not 'not eligible' — other regimes (e.g., EU law) may apply but are not evaluated by Recoup.

justification.reasoning: Part 260 covers flights 'to, from, or within the United States'.

cases.title: Travel credit: affirmative acceptance vs credit issued without the consumer's agreement

service_type.note: D253(3): recorded so this case's expected outcome is preserved; an unknown service type caps the result at likely eligible (R02-15)

expected.note: Affirmative acceptance of compensation in lieu of refund.

consumer_response.evidence: carrier email 'we have issued a travel credit to your account'; consumer took no action

deadline.semantics: 7 business days after 2026-10-15 (the cancelled flight's scheduled departure date, when non-response to the credit offer becomes a deemed request)

expected.note: A credit the carrier issued unilaterally is not acceptance.

justification.reasoning: 260.7: the carrier must not deem acceptance 'unless the consumer affirmatively agrees'. 260.6(a)(2)(iii)(B): non-response to a voucher offer by the cancelled flight's scheduled departure date makes the refund due.

cases.title: Flight merely renumbered (no time/airport/cabin change); consumer rejected the renumbered flight

expected.explanation: The regulation's text treats a renumbered flight as a cancellation, but DOT has announced it will not enforce the refund rules for renumbered flights with no significant change until 2027-07-07 while it reconsiders the definition (Refund III).

expected.note: The enforcement discretion expired and the rule pack has not been re-verified (30-day refresh; mandatory re-review by 2027-07-07).

justification.reasoning: Two first-party sources point different ways (regulatory text vs published enforcement discretion). Blocking only this conclusion with manual_review preserves both (mission §8).

cases.title: Same facts as R02-01 but the rule pack was last verified 48 days before the clock

expected.note: 48 days since verification > 30-day window. (M2D: clock moved after the R02-01 facts, per review R02.2.)

justification.reasoning: The mission §8 lifecycle requires verified, current sources before activation. Staleness blocks the conclusion, not the user's data.

expected.note: X5: no current source record for the pack.

cases.title: Duplicate evaluation of R02-01, with an overlapping card trip-cancellation benefit

expected.dedupe: reuse the existing opportunity; create no second opportunity or claim; identical fact snapshot → identical result

overlap.rule: The airline refund is the primary path. A card trip-cancellation benefit covers non-refundable costs, so a fare the airline must refund is not a non-refundable loss. Never add the two. R12 stays 'needs_facts' / 'possible_contract_benefit' until an exact card guide is identified.

justification.reasoning: Re-evaluation must be idempotent (mission §7 Claim/case: no multiple active cases for one remedy via repeated evaluation). Alternative recovery paths are not additive (mission §6).

cases.title: User says they rejected the change; the carrier's booking record shows the rebooking accepted (confirmed vs observed)

candidates.evidence: carrier booking record retrieved 2026-10-02 shows the rebooked flight XA202 ticketed

expected.explanation: You said you rejected the new schedule, but the airline's booking shows the rebooked flight ticketed to you. Check your airline messages (or ask the airline to cancel the rebooking) before a refund request is prepared.

justification.reasoning: Acceptance of rebooking is disqualifying; a confirmed statement contradicting the carrier's own record needs review.

cases.title: Public charter flight on R02-01's facts: not a covered flight (M27 erratum E-R02-1, D234(5))

service_type.evidence: booking confirmation: public charter operator disclosure

expected.note: A charter is not 'a scheduled flight', so it is not a covered flight under part 260 (spec §16 step 2, L13). 'Unsupported' is not 'not eligible': other rules may give a refund, but R02 v1 does not evaluate them.

justification.reasoning: A covered flight is 'a scheduled flight operated or marketed by a covered carrier'; a covered carrier is one 'conducting scheduled passenger service'; 260.6(a)(1) protects a consumer 'on a scheduled flight'. DOT's regulations name 'charter or scheduled passenger service' as separate kinds of service (254.2).
Any known non-scheduled service is outside the covered-flight definition.

amount.formula: fare + taxes + ancillary fees - already refunded

expected.note: A confirmed scheduled flight by a covered carrier: the result equals R02-01, which since lead ruling D253(3) records the same confirmed service type. With the service type unknown the result is capped (R02-15).

justification.reasoning: The covered-flight condition holds; the rest is R02-01.

expected.note: An unconfirmed extraction never gives 'unsupported' (D234(1)): the user is asked whether the flight was a charter.

justification.reasoning: A negative or out-of-scope verdict never rests on an unconfirmed candidate; the candidate is listed as candidate_unconfirmed.

cases.title: Service type unknown on R02-01's otherwise-eligible facts: capped at likely eligible with the labelled assumption (lead ruling D253(3))

amount.formula: fare + taxes + ancillary fees - already refunded

deadline.semantics: as R02-01; the service type is not the carrier timer's anchor, selector or zone (D234)

expected.question: Was this a regularly scheduled flight, or a charter or other non-scheduled flight?
expected.note: R02-01's facts with the service type unknown. Confirmed 'scheduled', the result is R02-01's (eligible); unknown, the covered-flight condition is not resolved toward eligible (D234(8)): the result is capped with the labelled assumption. The service type is asked because it is the only thing between likely and eligible (spec §16 step 8).

justification.reasoning: A covered flight is 'a scheduled flight operated or marketed by a covered carrier' (260.2), and 260.6(a)(1) protects a consumer 'on a scheduled flight'. With the service type unknown that condition is unknown. Lead ruling D253(3), no exception to README rule 5 ('unknown → capped at likely eligible with an explicit assumption'): capped at likely_eligible with the assumption 'assumes a regularly scheduled flight', and the question asked because every other decisive fact is R02-01's confirmed value.

service_type.note: the user answered that they do not know

amount.formula: fare + taxes + ancillary fees - already refunded

expected.note: The enum value 'unknown' is treated like a missing value: it is not a known non-scheduled value, so it gives the cap, not 'unsupported' (spec §5, §16 steps 2 and 8).

justification.reasoning: D253(3) speaks of an unknown service type; only a known non-scheduled value gives unsupported.

expected.note: Two things stand between likely and eligible (the unconfirmed fare and the unknown service type), so the service type is not asked yet; the assumption is still shown. Once the fare is confirmed, the case is R02-15 and the service type is asked (spec §16 step 8).

justification.reasoning: D253(3): the service-type question is asked when it is the only thing between likely and eligible; here the unconfirmed fare also is.

expected.note: An extracted 'scheduled' is not confirmed. service_type is on the spec §16 step 8 decisive list, so README cross-pack rule 1 (D147(2)) caps the outcome and asks for the confirmation, as for any other decisive fact (compare R02-01d).

justification.reasoning: Cross-pack rule 1: eligible requires every decisive fact to be confirmed; an extracted candidate caps the outcome at likely_eligible and the missing item is the confirmation.

cases.title: Known public charter on R02-04's facts (consumer's decision still unknown): unsupported before any eligibility question (lead ruling D253(3))

service_type.evidence: booking confirmation: public charter operator disclosure

expected.note: A known non-scheduled service decides applicability at spec §16 step 2, before the decision questions of steps 5–7, so the consumer's response is not asked (compare R02-04 → needs_facts [consumer_response]). 'Unsupported' is not 'not eligible': R02 v1 does not evaluate a charter.

justification.reasoning: A covered flight is 'a scheduled flight'; a covered carrier is one 'conducting scheduled passenger service'; 254.2 names 'charter or scheduled passenger service' separately. D253(3): a known non-scheduled value → unsupported.
